 Search "Summer Vacation" K-Drama Review: Is This Teen Romance Really a Healing Love Story?
 Disha Paul 11 hours ago 4 min read Summer Vacation : The new coming-of-age K-drama that challenges the idea of a perfect healing romance. (Wavve) A beautiful countryside, a summer romance, and two young people hoping to escape their ordinary lives. At first glance, Summer Vacation  sounds like the kind of Korean drama that will leave viewers feeling warm and comforted. But beneath its refreshing summer visuals lies a much more complicated story. 
 Starring Cho Yi-hyun and Jung Jin-young , the new teen romance is attracting attention for its emotionally complicated leads, difficult family environments, and a love triangle that is already raising questions. Rather than giving viewers two perfect people who heal each other through love, the drama introduces characters whose own problems could make their relationship far messier than expected. 
 If Summer Vacation  has caught your attention through Instagram clips, here is everything you need to know about its story, cast, episode schedule, and where to watch it. 
 Where to Watch Summer Vacation K-Drama 
 Summer Vacation  premiered on October 26, 2026 . The series airs in South Korea through Wavve and Lifetime, while international viewers can find its official streaming listing on Rakuten Viki. Streaming catalogues can vary by country. 
 Summer Vacation K-Drama: Episode Count and Release Schedule 
 The drama has 10 episodes , with new episodes scheduled for Mondays and Tuesdays.

 What Is Summer Vacation About? 
 Kim Ha-yeon ( Cho Yi-hyun ) is an 18-year-old high school student who feels disconnected from the people around her. Her family life offers little of the warmth she wants, while school leaves her feeling isolated. Instead of accepting her circumstances, she dreams of a life that feels more extraordinary, almost like the story of a movie protagonist. 
 Summer Vacation  (Wavve) Her summer takes an unexpected turn when she accompanies her father on a business trip to Upo Village. There, she meets Jo Yu-gyeom ( Jung Jin-young ), the eldest grandson of a prominent traditional family. He appears talented and composed, but his life is governed by strict expectations and old-fashioned rules that leave little room for personal freedom. 
 Their encounter introduces a new possibility into both their lives. Yet the village setting does not mean their problems will magically disappear. Ha-yeon and Yu-gyeom have their own emotional struggles, and the people already in Yu-gyeom's life make their growing connection more complicated. 
 Summer Vacation Cast: Who Plays Whom? 
 Cho Yi-hyun as Kim Ha-yeon:  An ordinary teenager who wants to change her destiny and escape the loneliness of her everyday life. 
 Jung Jin-young as Jo Yu-gyeom:  The gifted eldest grandson of a traditional family whose seemingly privileged life is controlled by expectations. 
 Hong Ye-ji as Sung Sae-ryeong:  Yu-gyeom's girlfriend, whose presence complicates the developing connection between the two leads. 
 Ryu Hae-jun as Kim Jeong-yeon:  A supporting character in Ha-yeon's story. 
 The main cast also includes actors portraying members of Yu-gyeom's family and the people surrounding the two teenagers in Upo Village. 
 Why Summer Vacation Feels Different From a Typical Healing K-Drama 
 1. The Countryside Is Beautiful, but the Characters Are Not Perfect 
 Many healing dramas use peaceful villages, comforting meals, kind neighbors, and slow romances to create a sense of escape. Summer Vacation  has the scenery for that kind of story, but its leads are far from emotionally settled. 
 Ha-yeon feels overlooked and longs for a different life. Yu-gyeom is trapped by a family structure that leaves him little control over his own choices. Their meeting may offer them a chance to change, but it does not instantly resolve the problems they carry. 
 That contrast makes the drama interesting. The countryside provides a change of scenery, not an automatic cure for loneliness or family conflict. 
 2. Both Leads Have Problems of Their Own 
 Ha-yeon is not simply a cheerful heroine waiting for someone to rescue her. Her dissatisfaction with her life shapes the way she approaches the people around her. Yu-gyeom, meanwhile, is not just a handsome, talented boy who needs to fall in love to become happy. 
 Both characters have desires that may clash with the expectations placed on them. Their relationship could help them understand themselves, but it could also expose their less appealing sides. 
 Stills from episode 1 of Summer Vacation (Wavve) This is where the drama has the potential to move beyond a familiar opposites-attract romance. The more interesting question is not whether the leads can save each other, but whether they can grow without expecting another person to fix everything. 
 3. The Love Triangle Is Already Complicating Things 
 One of the biggest talking points is that Yu-gyeom already has a girlfriend, Sung Sae-ryeong. That detail changes the way viewers approach his connection with Ha-yeon. 
 Some fans are uncomfortable with the possibility of a romance developing while Yu-gyeom is still in a relationship. It raises a fair question: will the drama treat the existing relationship seriously, or will Sae-ryeong simply become an obstacle between the main leads? 
 The answer will depend on how the story develops. A complicated love triangle can create meaningful conflict, but it needs to give every character a believable perspective rather than excusing hurtful choices just because the central couple has chemistry. 
 Is Summer Vacation Worth Watching? 
 If you enjoy teen romances with a mysterious element, complicated family relationships, and characters who are not immediately easy to love, Summer Vacation  may be worth adding to your watchlist. 
 Its strongest appeal is the contrast between the bright, nostalgic summer setting and the emotional difficulties facing its leads. The existing girlfriend storyline also gives viewers something to debate beyond whether the main couple looks good together. 
 However, viewers looking for a straightforward, comforting healing drama may find the romantic conflict frustrating, particularly if the story does not handle its characters' choices carefully. 
 Ultimately, Summer Vacation  has the ingredients for a coming-of-age romance about loneliness, freedom, and the people who enter our lives at unexpected moments. Whether it becomes a genuinely healing story will depend on what the characters learn from their mistakes, not simply on who ends up with whom. 
 Have you started watching Summer Vacation ? Do you think Ha-yeon and Yu-gyeom could help each other grow, or are you already concerned about the love triangle?
